prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1005; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck from behind while stopped at a traffic signal. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of loss. Police report obtained and reviewed.

Entry 3: Statements from the other driver, two independent witnesses, and scene photographs all agree on how the collision occurred. The vehicle was in the claimant's lane and was struck at moderate speed by the trailing vehicle.

Entry 4: Police and both witnesses confirm the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time of impact. No conflicting information has been received on this point.

Entry 5: Medical records received from the claimant's treating providers document a concussion. The reported symptoms and the force of the impact are consistent with one another. No prior injury to the same body area is known from the file or from the claimant's history given so far.

Entry 6: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this type of injury. Requested updated records and a treatment timeline from counsel to understand the reasons for the extended care.

Entry 7: Claimant has added some smaller details to the account since the first interview, but the core description of events has not changed. Repair estimate reviewed; it is not yet clear whether all listed damage resulted from this impact, so the vehicle has been referred for a closer inspection.

Entry 8: A neighbor has told the field representative that the vehicle appeared damaged a few weeks before the claimed loss date. This has not been verified and is being noted for follow-up. No earlier damage to the vehicle is recorded in the file at this time, and the claim remains under review.
